{{Term/Store|Mushroom|Mushrooms|Series, ALttP, BotW, AoI|plural}} are recurring [[Item]]s and [[Object]]s in {{TLoZ Series}}.<ref name="E 132"/><ref name="BotW Nellie"/><ref name="AoI Materials"/>

==Location and Uses==
==={{ALttP|-}}===
{{Descriptions ALttP}}
[[File:ALttP Mushroom Inventory Sprite.png|left]]
In {{ALttP}}, the Mushroom can be found within the [[Lost Woods]]. [[Link]] can offer it to the [[Syrup|Witch]] in exchange for the [[Magic Powder]].

==={{LA|-}}===
{{Main|Sleepy Toadstool}}
[[File:LADX Mysterious Forest Toadstool.png|thumb|left|{{Game Label|{{LADX|-}}}}The location of the Toadstool]]
In {{LA}}, the Toadstool is found in the [[Mysterious Forest]]. It can be given to [[Syrup]] to be made into Magic Powder.
{{Clear|left}}

==={{OoT|-}}===
{{Main|Odd Mushroom}}
In {{OoT}}, the [[Odd Mushroom]] is part of the [[Trading Quest]]. [[Grog]] gives it to [[Link]] in exchange for [[Cojiro]].

==={{MM|-}}===
{{Main|Magic Mushroom}}
In {{MM}}, a Magic Mushroom can be sold to the [[Magic Hags' Potion Shop]] for 20 [[Rupee]]s each; at least one must be delivered during that cycle before [[Blue Potion]]s can be purchased there. They can also be sold to the [[Curiosity Shop]] for 5 Rupees each.

==={{OoS|-}}===
[[File:OoS Link Obtaining the Mushroom.png|Link receiving the Mushroom in {{OoS|-}}|thumb|left]]
In {{OoS}}, a Mushroom appears as an [[Item]] in the [[Trading Game]]. Using the [[Megaphone]], Link can wake up [[Talon]] in a cave atop [[Mt. Cucco]]. In exchange for waking him, Talon offers Link a Mushroom, which can in turn be given to [[Syrup]] in [[Sunken City]] in exchange for the [[Wooden Bird]].<ref>{{Cite|Sniff, sniff!!! That scent!!! Ya've got a Mushroom! I'll trade my Wooden Bird!|Syrup|OoS}}</ref>

[[Rock Mushroom]]s are a type of Mushroom that appear as obstacles.
{{Clear|left}}

==={{TWW|-}}===
Mushrooms commonly appear in [[Cave]]s, where they grow on the floors. They cannot be interacted with.

==={{TMC|-}}===
{{Main|Elastic Mushroom, Wake-Up Mushroom}}
[[File:TMC Elastic Mushroom Sprite 2.png|left]]
In {{TMC}}, the Wake-Up Mushroom is required for Link to obtain the [[Pegasus Boots]].

Elastic Mushrooms can also be found in certain areas while Link is shrunk to [[Minish]]-sized. The [[Gust Jar]] can be used to suck and pull back the Mushroom caps, which will then throw Link once released.

==={{TP|-}}===
Mushrooms appear in the [[Forest Temple (Twilight Princess)|Forest Temple]]. They cannot be interacted with.

==={{SS|-}}===
{{Main|Mushroom Spores}}
[[File:Fungal Spores.png|Link obtaining Mushroom Spores in {{SS|-}}|thumb]]
In {{SS}}, Mushrooms can be found in the [[Faron Woods#Skyward Sword|Faron Woods]], [[Deep Woods]], [[Skyview Temple]], and on certain islands in the [[Sky]]. Link can slash them with his [[Sword]] to produce [[Mushroom Spores]], which can be stored in Bottles and used to heal [[Loftwing]]s. Glittering Mushrooms can also be found, which produce [[Glittering Spores]] than can also be stored in Bottles. They produce different kind of effects when used on [[Item]]s and [[Enemy|Enemies]].

==={{BotW|-}}===
In {{BotW}}, Mushrooms are a type of [[Material]] that Link can collect for cooking [[Food]] or in some cases [[Enhancing]] [[Armor]]. Mushrooms are typically found on the ground growing next to [[Tree]]s or cliffs. Available mushrooms are [[Hylian Shroom]]s, [[Endura Shroom]]s, [[Stamella Shroom]]s, [[Hearty Truffle]]s, [[Big Hearty Truffle]]s, [[Chillshroom]]s, [[Sunshroom]]s, [[Zapshroom]]s, [[Rushroom]]s, [[Razorshroom]]s, [[Ironshroom]]s, and [[Silent Shroom]]s.

==={{TotK|-}}===
{{Frameless|[[File:TotK Giant Enoki Mushroom Plant Model.png|thumb|right|x200px|A Giant Enoki Mushroom Plant from {{TotK|-}}]]}}
Mushroom-like [[Tree]]s known as [[Giant Enoki Mushroom Plant]]s can be found in the [[Depths]]. The entrance to [[Hateno Village]] features prominent Mushroom designs, with [[Ventest Clothing Boutique]] changing its branding to feature Mushrooms. Several characters can also be seen wearing Mushroom hats.

==Trivia==
*In {{LA|-}}, the Mushroom is one of many {{smw|Mario (series)|''Mario''}} references. When Tarin (who bears resemblance to {{smw|Mario}}, and also shares his love of mushrooms) eats one, he turns into a raccoon, which may be a reference to Mario's {{smw|Raccoon Mario|Raccoon}} or {{smw|Tanooki Mario|Tanooki}} transformations.
